gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the tickets overpriced, but the seating was appalling.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only' at the front inverts the verb: Not only were the tickets… but…

gaps.sentence: The restaurant is famous ___ its seafood.
I couldn't reach the shelf, ___ how tall I am.
The findings will be published in ___ course.
gaps.hint: in ___ course = at the right time
gaps.explanation: 'In due course' = eventually, when the time is right.

gaps.sentence: He denied the charge, but the jury found him ___ after only an hour.
gaps.explanation: 'But' signals a contrast with his denial: the jury found him guilty.

gaps.sentence: She made the cake ___, without any help at all.
gaps.explanation: 'She made it herself' — the reflexive stresses she did it alone.

gaps.sentence: The athlete was banned ___ competing for two years.
gaps.explanation: 'Ban somebody from doing something' is the fixed pattern.
